title: Recruit and engage at least 2 qualified per-script reviewers or a language organization
context: Every scheme requires a qualified per-script reviewer sign-off, and the first scheme in each new script family requires a second independent reviewer. Without reviewers secured, Devanagari and Arabic scheme tasks cannot proceed. Reviewers may be individuals (linguists, native script users with transliteration competence) or a language/translation organization. Reviewer availability is an explicit project risk (PLAN.md risks table).
objective: Identify, contact, and confirm at least 2 qualified per-script reviewers (or an equivalent language/translation organization) willing to review Elyos open-transliteration schemes per the qualification criteria in reviewers-001. Record confirmed reviewers in docs/reviewers/roster.yaml with their script coverage, qualification basis, COI status, and contact/engagement terms.
acceptanceCriteria: At least 2 named qualified reviewers confirmed (or 1 organization committing equivalent reviewer coverage) and recorded in docs/reviewers/roster.yaml

Each roster entry records: reviewer id, name (or org name), script(s) covered, qualification basis (native/near-native + linguistic competence), COI status, engagement terms (volunteer/paid/org-delegated), and confirmation date
Reviewers meet the criteria defined in reviewers-001 (native/near-native script command + linguistic/transliteration competence per script pair)

Outreach approach and candidate list documented (even if some candidates declined); named target types include: Wikimedia language-tool contributors, library/GLAM cataloguing professionals, NLP researchers, language-revitalization NGO staff, linguistics academics
Result recorded as a deliverable document: docs/reviewers/reviewer-engagement-report.md summarizing outreach, outcomes, and roster status
resources: PLAN.md — Governance section; Open questions (reviewer sourcing)
Candidate types: Wikimedia language tooling contributors, library/GLAM professionals, Unicode CLDR contributors, NLP researchers, language NGOs
